meta.title: LingoLinq Launch Readiness Requirements
meta.description: Strategy-layer requirement matrix for the Compliance & Launch Readiness dashboard. Encodes the direct requirements for each launch milestone. This file NEVER overrides audit-reports/FINDINGS.json, which remains canonical for finding lifecycle (status, severity, disposition, closure evidence).
meta.governance: Only Scot ratifies this matrix, changes humanStatus governance semantics, marks a requirement accepted-for-milestone, or flips meta.ratification. Scripts and agents may propose edits via PR but never self-ratify. accepted-risk or disposition=accepted in the findings register NEVER implies accepted-for-milestone here.

ratification.note: PROPOSED - requires Scot ratification. Every humanStatus, blocking flag, and appliesWhen interpretation below is a proposal until ratification.

milestones.title: Public MVP
milestones.inheritanceNote: Inherits applicable UNRESOLVED blockers only; school-beta inheritance is conditional on the mvpIncludesMinors launch-profile decision.

milestones.title: District Procurement Ready
milestones.inheritanceNote: May inherit public-mvp blockers if policy requires; not enabled in v0.2.

meta.appliesWhenSemantics: appliesWhen.decisions lists LAUNCH-PROFILE.json decision keys gating applicability (any-of: requirement applies if any listed decision is true). If none is true and at least one is 'undecided', the derived status is decision-needed. Empty list = always applies. appliesWhen.summary is the human-readable condition.
meta.findingSemantics: findingIds must exist in audit-reports/FINDINGS.json (validated; read-only cross-reference). findingScope is a prose description of an aggregate finding class (e.g. launch-relevant WCAG Mediums) that cannot be pinned to specific IDs. Invariants compute over FINDINGS.json each generation and never store completion status.

requirements.text: No unresolved Critical finding affects the selected beta configuration.
requirements.whyItMatters: A controlled beta should not proceed with a known unresolved Critical affecting the cohort.

requirements.text: Raw communication is not retained in an unsafe pre-scrubber or process-global AI cache.

appliesWhen.summary: runtime AI word prediction is enabled

requirements.whyItMatters: AAC utterances may contain highly sensitive communication content and must not be retained outside the intended minimization boundary.

requirements.text: Unreadable or invalid AI master preference fails closed.
requirements.whyItMatters: Unknown consent intent must not be converted into permission.

requirements.text: Focus-word generation enforces user, organization, COPPA, EU-under-16, and applicable disclosure gates before a cache hit can return AI output.
requirements.whyItMatters: Cached AI output must not bypass consent and child-protection controls.

requirements.text: Required direct-interaction AI disclosure is presented and enforced for covered users before the covered interaction occurs.
requirements.findingScope: LL-a9d6d5a46b applies where the disclosure surface is rendered

appliesWhen.summary: jurisdiction and feature combination requires Article 50 or equivalent disclosure

requirements.whyItMatters: Transparency obligations must work in the actual runtime path, not only exist in code.

requirements.text: Required Terms/consent flow is reachable with switch scanning for the beta cohort.
requirements.whyItMatters: A switch-scanning AAC user must not be trapped at a mandatory modal.

requirements.text: Intro/onboarding cannot replace required Terms before the user has had the opportunity to review and agree.

appliesWhen.summary: Terms is required for the user/session

requirements.whyItMatters: Required consent presentation cannot be silently skipped by modal ordering.

requirements.text: Controlled beta deploys use a verified release process that cannot falsely pass the wrong revision or silently deploy stale/unapproved code.
requirements.whyItMatters: Beta reliability and assurance depend on knowing exactly what code was released and verified.

requirements.text: Core communication controls used by the beta cohort are operable and programmatically understandable with the applicable access methods and assistive technology.
requirements.findingScope: aggregate: launch-relevant WCAG Mediums and Highs

appliesWhen.summary: always; exact modalities depend on cohort

requirements.whyItMatters: Accessibility failures on core AAC communication paths are product-readiness failures, not peripheral polish.

requirements.text: Known failures capable of materially breaking core board, speech, image, sync, or communication workflows for the beta cohort are remediated and verified under representative use.
requirements.findingScope: aggregate: launch-relevant reliability findings including remediated-unverified items
requirements.whyItMatters: A supervised beta still requires reliable core communication and data-preservation paths.

requirements.text: A parent/guardian consent path exists and functions for children who require it.
requirements.whyItMatters: Child participation cannot depend on an implied or missing guardian authorization path.

requirements.text: District seat reclaim/offboarding cannot silently convert an under-13 child into a consumer trial without required re-consent or a defined lawful transition.
requirements.whyItMatters: School-to-family transition is a high-risk lifecycle boundary for COPPA and notice obligations.

requirements.text: Declined or expired parental consent leads to a safe, defined account/data outcome rather than indefinite ambiguous access.
requirements.whyItMatters: Expired or declined consent must have a deterministic privacy-preserving lifecycle.

requirements.text: Hard deletion includes UserVideo and standalone/off-board voice recordings and other covered media.
requirements.whyItMatters: Deletion claims are incomplete if sensitive media survives as orphaned rows/objects.

requirements.text: A school/district organization can disable covered third-party AI processing for its users.
requirements.whyItMatters: Districts need a meaningful tenant-level control over optional AI processing.

requirements.text: COPPA/minor AI restrictions are enforced server-side and cannot be bypassed by direct API use or cached output.
requirements.findingScope: related AI consent findings where applicable
requirements.whyItMatters: Child-protection policy must be an enforcement boundary, not UI-only guidance.

requirements.text: School-sponsored account authorization, notice basis, ownership, and transition lifecycle are documented and operationally coherent.
requirements.whyItMatters: District and family responsibilities must be clear before real school-managed users are onboarded.

requirements.text: Parent/student/Terms/consent flows are usable with the relevant AAC access methods for the cohort.
requirements.whyItMatters: A compliant consent path that an AAC user cannot operate is not a usable consent path.

requirements.text: Public privacy, AI, processor, retention, and data-flow disclosures match production behavior and current architecture.
requirements.whyItMatters: Customer-facing claims must describe the system that actually runs.

requirements.text: The serving Bedrock credential is demonstrably tied to the BAA-covered AWS account when Bedrock is enabled.
requirements.whyItMatters: Contract coverage is not sufficient unless the actual serving credential is proven to belong to the covered account.

requirements.text: Production deploy cannot falsely pass an old revision, silently use stale/unapproved code, or bypass the intended release authorization path.
requirements.whyItMatters: Public launch requires repeatable, attributable release assurance.

requirements.text: Seed/test/admin credentials are rotated, removed, disabled, or converted to a governed break-glass posture before customer-facing use.
requirements.whyItMatters: A memorable seeded admin credential is incompatible with customer-ready privileged access.

requirements.text: All launch-relevant High remediated-unverified findings that apply to the launch configuration have completed required verification or reconciliation.
requirements.whyItMatters: Public MVP should not treat 'code probably fixed' as equivalent to verified closure for launch-relevant Highs.

requirements.text: Incident/breach runbook matches current runtime/vendor architecture and is operationally usable.
requirements.whyItMatters: Response procedures must point responders to current systems, providers, and recovery paths.

requirements.text: A current district-facing trust packet exists and customer-facing documents agree with production.
requirements.whyItMatters: District reviewers need a coherent packet, not a collection of inconsistent source documents.

requirements.text: Subprocessors, purposes, data categories, contracts, AI providers, and notice posture are current and internally consistent.
requirements.whyItMatters: Vendor diligence depends on a complete and truthful subprocessor/data-flow inventory.

requirements.text: Retention/deletion schedule is documented and the material lifecycle controls are operationally verified.
requirements.whyItMatters: Districts increasingly ask not only what retention is promised but how it is technically enforced.

requirements.text: Districts can understand what AI is used, what data is sent, who processes it, what controls exist, what retention applies, and how AI can be disabled.
requirements.whyItMatters: AI procurement review increasingly requires clear data-flow and governance answers.

requirements.text: Core AAC paths have documented automated/manual accessibility testing, known limitations, and remediation status.
requirements.whyItMatters: District accessibility review requires evidence beyond informal claims.

requirements.text: Customer-facing incident/breach summary, contacts, notification posture, and response process are current.
requirements.whyItMatters: Procurement teams need a credible operational response posture.

requirements.text: Production email authentication and domain alignment are verified for the customer-facing mail path.
requirements.whyItMatters: Password reset, consent, and school communications depend on trustworthy authenticated mail.

requirements.text: Dependency scanning, secret scanning, code-quality gates, repository controls, and vulnerability response operate continuously.
requirements.whyItMatters: District security review increasingly examines software supply-chain assurance.

requirements.text: Required import/export/admin interoperability for the intended deployment model is documented and tested.
requirements.whyItMatters: Interoperability is increasingly a procurement and implementation criterion.

requirements.text: Produce a formal VPAT/ACR when commercially appropriate.
requirements.whyItMatters: Formal accessibility conformance reporting may become a procurement expectation.

requirements.text: Complete SOC 2 or equivalent independent control assurance when buyer pressure and company stage justify it.
requirements.whyItMatters: SOC 2 may become valuable evidence but is not the immediate launch finish line.

requirements.text: Mature privileged access with MFA, centralized auditability, least privilege, and governed break-glass.
requirements.whyItMatters: Strong privileged-access governance reduces insider and operator risk.

requirements.text: Retention schedules are technically enforced and monitored across relevant data classes.
requirements.whyItMatters: Manual or partial retention enforcement does not scale with customer growth.

requirements.text: Mature SIEM/WAF/central monitoring/alerting and security-operations practices are in place.
requirements.whyItMatters: Continuous detection and operational response become more important as scale and threat exposure grow.

requirements.text: Access/deletion/request workflows are scalable, auditable, and operationally repeatable.
requirements.whyItMatters: Manual DSAR handling becomes fragile at scale.

requirements.text: Periodic independent penetration, accessibility, privacy, and evidence-refresh testing is established.
requirements.whyItMatters: Independent validation reduces blind spots and stale assurance claims.
